searchText: https://gist.github.com/zsfelfoldi/9607ad248707a925b701f49787904fd6 can a baseFee be 0 ? Not with the current specifications. It can only go down to 7 Wei so 6 Wei is an exception ? (i mean shall throw an exception) Not sure what you mean with exception. If you mean "rare", then no. If you mean "impossible" or "error", then yes. hm. is it in EIP paper? Afaik it's only in there implicitly, and some statements later on that allude to it being able to become zero (wrongly so). The spec might have been updated since though. No, but only as a side effect. It isn't something that should be tested *directly*. That is, it isn't a behavior that we need and if a change elsewhere were to result in us being able to reach 0 that would be totally fine. What *should* be tested is the behavior of what happens when the parent base fee is 7 and empty. Same with 8 (another boundary condition). And if it were me I would have tests for parent base_fee 0 and 1 as well (even though currently we can't ever get to them, the behavior should that ever change is well defined). <@439556036647714817> All the tests we have are legacy transactions so I wanted to run them on a header with baseFee 0 is that ok? It depends on the clients. It's not forbidden by the EIP, but it's not ever going to happen (in real life), so relying on it could bite us in the future. I think it's OK to do it for now, but remember this if a client has a problem with almost all our tests. An alternative solution would be if `blockHeader` / `env` doesn't have a `baseFee` to specify `baseFee: 0x10` (for example) and add (implicitly) to every transaction `tip: <gasPrice> - 0x10`
